newsitem.title: PERU: Shell says $1 bln Peru ethylene plant possible. [CORRECTED 17:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Shell says $1 bln Peru ethylene plant possible. [CORRECTED 17:30 GMT]

text.p: Shell Prospecting and Development (Peru) B.V. said building a $1 billion ethylene plant to take ethane from its Camisea hydrocarbon reserves in Peru was an "exciting possibility".
(Corrects from "said it was building a..." to "said building a..." to make clear that the company finds the prospect of building a plant exciting, but that it is not yet building a plant.)
Shell is a unit of the Anglo-Dutch Royal Dutch/Shell group.

Mid-way through a license to study the reserves for the exploitation of gas, Shell had also realized it was "feasible" to extract 850,000 tonnes per year of ethane, the company's managing director in Peru, Alan Hunt, added in a weekend interview.
"We could find ourselves investing in chemicals but it could also be a third party," Hunt said. "Economically it looks attractive. It just needs enthusiasm from a (company) to go ahead."
In addition to any possible investment in a chemical plant, Shell -- the operating partner of a joint venture with Mobil -- plans to invest up to $3 billion developing the huge Camisea reserves.
